newsitem.title: USA: Sudbury stock jumps on Intermet takeover.
newsitem.headline: Sudbury stock jumps on Intermet takeover.

text.p: The stock of Sudbury Inc. rose in heavy trading Tuesday, a day after the Cleveland-based automotive and industrial supplier agreed to be acquired by Intermet Corp. for $195 million.

Sudbury rose $2.125 to $12.125 at midday on the Nasdaq market, where more than 1.1 million shares changed hands. Intermet, a ferrous casting foundry company and automotive supplier, gained 75 cents to $13, also on Nasdaq.

On Tuesday, the companies announced a definitive merger agreement under which Intermet will begin a cash tender offer of $12.50 a share for all of Sudbury's 15.6 million outstanding shares, on a diluted basis.
"It looks like a clearcut deal" that has the blessing of Sudbury management, Jerry Dombcik, director of research at McDonald & Co., said.
"It doesn't preclude somebody coming in with a higher offer, but I don't think it's likely."
Mark Brody, Sudbury's chief financial officer, said tender offer documents to be sent out within five days will outline when the offer will commence and other details.
